clue.text: Steamship in a lake? Quite the opposite when making a TV show

indicators.note: the surface puts the ship inside the water, so one item sits within another
this flips the stated arrangement, so the outer and inner items swap roles

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for a steamship
Lake Erie, one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A puzzling image of a steamer afloat on a lake, oddly tied to producing a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'steamship in lake', then 'Quite the opposite' reverses it: the lake goes inside the ship, giving S(ERIE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a run of episodes making up a television programme, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Chuckle after comics ultimately kill

indicators.note: after puts the laugh behind the chosen letter in the answer
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of comics is used

parts.note: the final letter of comics
a chuckle is a burst of quiet laughter

explanation.surface: A comedian 'killing' the audience, the chuckles that follow a good set.
explanation.walkthrough: Comics speak of killing when a show goes well, which makes 'kill' look like stage slang rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is a verb meaning to kill brutally or in large numbers.

clue.text: Orator's regret over insult in argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the first piece comes on top
an orator speaks, so the word that follows is taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: A public speaker apologising for an insult made during a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang a rhubarb is a noisy squabble, especially a row on a baseball field.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is US slang for a heated dispute or brawl, so it can stand for a quarrel.

clue.text: Transitory things are mediocre gym mounts

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that mounts climbs upward, so the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
meh is a slang verdict for something unexciting and mediocre
PE, physical education, is school gym class

explanation.surface: Remarks that the vaulting horses at the gym are second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym mounts' looks like apparatus such as horses, but mounts climbs upward and reverses all three pieces in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that last only a short time, from the Greek for lasting a day.

clue.text: Style accessory is small and brittle

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
something brittle breaks with a crunch

explanation.surface: A fashion item described as tiny and easily snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrunchy is a fabric-covered elastic band used to style and hold back hair.

clue.text: Shut up about malfunctioning Dell, subject to flickering illumination

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: can it is slang for be quiet

indicators.note: a malfunctioning machine is out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Telling a broken Dell computer to be quiet while its screen flickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something candlelit is lit by candles, whose flames flicker.

clue.text: At last! Ecru-black combination that can be applied

indicators.note: at last points at the closing letter only, so the next word gives just its end

parts.note: the final letter of ecru
sable is a heraldic and poetic word for black

explanation.surface: A decorator thrilled to find a cream-and-black paint mix ready to brush on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last!' reads as an exclamation of relief, but it only selects the last letter of Ecru.
explanation.definitionFit: Usable means fit to be put to use, and applied here means put to use.

clue.text: Male involved in escapade is not as dear

indicators.note: someone involved in a scheme is caught up inside it

parts.note: a caper is a mischievous escapade
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a prank is less beloved for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' reads as beloved, but here it means expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear can mean costly, so something less dear has a lower price.

clue.text: Hitched very well in the old road on the right

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
OK means all right, very well

indicators.note: the right-hand side of a written word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of road

explanation.surface: Married long ago and well matched, on the right side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Ye Olde Shoppe style signs use YE for the, so 'the old' gives YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoked means joined together like oxen under a yoke, and hitched means joined, including in marriage.

clue.text: Insulting remark one might find in a musical score

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a disparaging slight on someone's reputation

definitions.text: one might find in a musical score
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a curved mark telling the player to join notes smoothly

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a phrase describing something on sheet music; the same short word fits it and an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both a derogatory remark and the notation arc binding notes legato.

clue.text: George and Gregory hugging antelope as a measure of love?

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap your arms around it, so the two names go round the animal

parts.note: a George, as in a George Bush, the US president's surname with the article
a Gregory, as in a Gregory Peck, the film actor's surname with the article
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: Two famous men embracing an antelope, offered as a way of quantifying affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Each forename stands for 'a Bush' and 'a Peck' (George Bush, Gregory Peck), and the pair hug ELAND between them. The phrase comes from the Guys and Dolls song 'I love you a bushel and a peck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushels and pecks are old dry-volume units, and the song uses them as an amount of affection, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Lightweight to damage set of rules

parts.note: a gram is a very small unit of weight
to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: A lightweight boxer or politician out to wreck the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the system of rules governing how a language is structured.

clue.text: Boy grabs ruined one-ply leaf

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so the boy word closes round what follows

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy snatching a damaged sheet of single-layer tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-ply' looks like a single tissue, but it splits into I for one and the word ply, which are mixed up and placed inside LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily.

clue.text: Bill, before eating salt in a place of worship

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: something that eats takes the next item inside itself

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
NaCl is the chemical formula of common salt

explanation.surface: Settling a restaurant bill before a salty meal inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt here is chemistry: NaCl, sodium chloride, sits inside ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a building or tent used for religious worship.

clue.text: Retro high-school dance hosted in a residence that's unfinished and shapeless

indicators.note: hosted in means the reversed dance is held inside the other letters, as guests are in a home
that's unfinished means the word for residence loses its final letter

parts.note: a house is a residence

indicators.note: Retro, read as backwards-looking, means the word for the dance is reversed

parts.note: a prom is an American high-school formal dance

explanation.surface: A vintage-themed school dance is held in a half-built house that has no real form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' looks like a style for the dance, but it is the reversal signal; 'hosted in' then puts the reversed dance inside A plus the shortened house, so 'unfinished' belongs to the residence, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorphous means lacking a definite form or structure, a direct synonym of shapeless.

clue.text: In the end, roast zebra is not kosher

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept from the word next to it

parts.note: the final letter of roast
in the US a referee is nicknamed a zebra for the striped shirt

explanation.surface: Roasted zebra meat, unsurprisingly, fails Jewish dietary law.
explanation.walkthrough: The zebra is not the animal: American sports referees wear black-and-white stripes and are called zebras.
explanation.definitionFit: Tref is the Yiddish term for food forbidden under Jewish dietary law, the opposite of kosher.

clue.text: Comments placed atop of mirror image

definitions.meaning: surface reading: remarks written at the head of a page
setter's reading: the remarks sit at the opposite of the top, the bottom of the page

explanation.walkthrough: Reflect 'atop' in a mirror and you get its opposite, the bottom, which is where these comments are printed.
explanation.definitionFit: These are notes printed at the bottom of a page, explaining or citing the text above.

clue.text: One way to cook eggs — or, by the sound of it, where they're made empty?

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word that is heard the same as another

parts.note: eggs are produced in the ovaries, which are left empty once the eggs are released

explanation.surface: A breakfast order that doubles as an anatomy joke about where eggs come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the cooking term sounds close to the organs that produce eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs fried over easy are flipped and cooked briefly so the yolk stays runny.

clue.text: Not Common Era (looking back after start of Renaissance)

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the chosen initial in the answer
the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Renaissance

indicators.note: to look back is to face the other way, so the word is read from its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A historian's aside distinguishing BC from the Common Era, glancing back to the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common Era' looks like one dating term, but the definition takes only 'Not Common' and leaves Era to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom found or occurring, the opposite of common.

clue.text: Pasta with red sauce containing a bit of veal

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for red

indicators.note: a sauce containing something holds it inside

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise sauce

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of veal

explanation.surface: An Italian dinner of pasta in tomato sauce with some veal in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red sauce' looks like one item, marinara, but red gives only R and the sauce is aioli.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is a type of pasta made of small filled square pockets.

clue.text: Capital card game on tape

parts.note: monte, as in three-card monte, is a gambling card game
a videotape is often just called a video

explanation.surface: A first-rate card game recorded on videotape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent, but it is a noun: a nation's seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Montevideo is the capital city of Uruguay.

clue.text: Tonic I'd brewed, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describing a tonic they brewed, as a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is a person's style of enunciation and choice of words when speaking.

clue.text: Charity receives nothing on time, practically

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the time piece comes after
to receive something is to take it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
O looks like zero, nothing
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A charity getting no donations, nearly on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly, and practically is used in the same sense of very nearly.

clue.text: Cultivate hybrid, finally, with someone who ate an apple and prune

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the closing letter of hybrid
in Genesis Eve eats the forbidden fruit, traditionally an apple
to lop is to cut off branches, to prune

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: breed a hybrid with Eve's help, then trim it back.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop something is to grow or foster it, which is what cultivate means figuratively.

clue.text: Blockheads posed awkwardly

indicators.note: done awkwardly means arranged clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Stupid people standing stiffly for a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopes and blockheads are both informal words for stupid people.

clue.text: US citizen replacing me with force of another continent

indicators.note: replacing one thing with another means swapping a part out and putting the new part in its place

parts.note: a citizen of the United States
taken as written, the letters to be removed
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A US citizen swapping himself out for some force from another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' reads as the speaker, but it is just two letters inside the citizen word; F is the physics symbol for force.
explanation.definitionFit: African is the adjective for things belonging to Africa, a continent other than America.

clue.text: How cute! Roy's disheartened and wrong

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letter goes

parts.note: aw is the sound people make at something sweet
the name Roy, which is disheartened

explanation.surface: Someone cooing at a sad Roy, who has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy's is Roy is: he is the one disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, so things gone wrong have gone awry.

clue.text: World War II leader divides noodle-soup vessel with elite shooter

indicators.note: something that divides a thing sits between its parts, splitting it in two

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup
an urn is a vase-like vessel
Hideki Tojo was Japan's prime minister during the Second World War
the A-list is the most celebrated group

explanation.surface: A wartime leader splitting a bowl of noodle soup with a top sniper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooter' looks like it pairs with elite as a sniper, but it is the definition on its own: someone who shoots with a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A photojournalist tells news stories through photographs, and photographers are informally called shooters.

clue.text: Nervous and playful?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: jumpy, easily alarmed, like a startled horse
second meaning: lively and frisky in a capricious way

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that one word covers both moods, jittery and frolicsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish describes an animal easily startled, and also a person who is flighty, frivolous or frisky.

clue.text: "The Swan": overture and finale of choreography performed in reverse order

indicators.note: the overture opens and the finale closes, so only the first and last letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of choreography

indicators.note: reverse order means reading the word from back to front

parts.note: a song that is performed is sung

explanation.surface: A programme note for a ballet called The Swan, its choreography staged backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Swan' looks like a ballet or Saint-Saens's cello piece, but it is the meaning of a Latin star name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnus is the northern constellation whose Latin name means swan.
